findings.reason: a worker implementing §23 as written reaches a case it cannot satisfy and must either drop the pinned-behaviour test or leave a day-parsing rule inside one of the three readers, contradicting the section's own single-parser and unchanged-behaviour claims.
findings.text: §23's change text says `telemetry_store._ladder_stem`, `serving_receipts._roll_date` and `serving_receipts._record_stem_and_suffix` "all call it, and none of them parses the day itself", while the same section at :868 states the three disagree on suffixed names and the done-when at :877 requires each to still return its former result and "Behaviour does not change" (:869). Measured on the merged code (`886fc21c`): for `foo-1.20261015.jsonl.gz` the three return `None`, `('foo-1', '.jsonl.gz')` and `'foo-1.20261015.jsonl'` respectively — `_ladder_stem` recognises a day only in the second-to-last position while the sibling `_record_stem_and_suffix` recognises it anywhere before `.jsonl`. A single (stem, day, suffix) split fixes one recognition rule, so under the §23 change either `_record_stem_and_suffix` loses its stem `foo-1` or `_ladder_stem` loses `foo-1.20261015.jsonl`; both cannot hold, so the done-when test cannot pass and the "the eight-digit day pattern in that function only" search cannot be satisfied

response_events.reason: s23 revised (c4973a7d): the parser owns only the day match; each reader keeps its own suffix rule against the parser's fields, so every former result holds on receipt names. The done-when pins four names with the compressed segment's expected results.
